newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX makes sharp gains with tough week ahead.
newsitem.headline: German DAX makes sharp gains with tough week ahead.

text.p: German shares on Tuesday moved sharply higher to new record levels and were expected to see further support from the dollar over a week set to include a number of market-moving events both in Germany and the U.S.
The IBIS-DAX electronic trade index stood 79.06 points up at 3,337.80 by 1517 GMT on Tuesday because of the stronger dollar and an earlier rally among car stocks.

"But I doubt that by the end of the week it will be holding anywhere near to 3,350 points," said on trader, noting that, aside from U.S. Federal Reserve Alan Greespan's congressional testimony Wendesday, a slew of economic data was due.
Other main market focuses include German GDP data due Wednesday and German February unemployment figures on Thursday.
Dealers said the market had factored in a rise to 4.7 million jobless from the 4.66 million reported for January. Such a figure was cited in the mass circulation Bild newspaper on Tuesday.

Following bullish noises from Mercedes-manufacturer Daimler-Benz out of the Geneva car-show late Monday, dealers said it was likely that further upbeat business statements could emerge from the show over the week, which in turn could have a continued strong impact on the DAX index.
